title: Virender Sehwag Gives His Verdict On Workload Management: 'Important For Bowlers...' | Cricket News - News18
text: India’s recent England tour will be remembered for some time to come given how the Shubman Gill-led side showed terrific fight to draw the five-match series 2-2. There were several eye-catching individual performances throughout the campaign which has given an indication that the future of Indian Test cricket is in safe hands following the retirements of Virat Kohli, Rohit Sharma, Ravichandran Ashwin. One of the hotly debated topics during and after the series was that of workload management with pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah at the center of it. As part of their plan, the Indian team management played the injury-prone fast bowler in three of the five matches despite him being fit. The 31-year-old played in the first, third and fourth Tests. Trailing England 1-2, India were in a must-win situation in the fifth and final Test at The Oval which Bumrah skipped. On the other hand, Mohammed Siraj played in all five Tests. The decision to stick to their plan invited criticism from some quarters. Now, batting legend Virender Sehwag has shared his verdict on the relevance of workload management in the sport – the former India opener reckons that it’s important, especially for the fast bowlers but not for batters. “I think workload is important, especially for bowlers. For batsmen, I don’t think workload is a problem, since they can play and don’t have to play too many matches anyway. So, I think it’s important mainly for bowlers, especially fast bowlers," Sehwag said on Sony Sports Network . “If they are managed properly, they can play for a longer time. For India, it’s important that all fast bowlers stay fit, because in big events like the Asia Cup or World Cup, if they are available, India’s chances of winning will be higher," he added. There were speculations about Bumrah’s availability for the Asia Cup, scheduled to begin on September 9. However, these rumours were dispelled after the 31-year-old was announced as part of India’s 15-player squad.
